section.title: Introduction
section.para: The search order of a bundle class loader is determined by the wiring of the bundle. Extensions that want to make more classes or resources visible to a bundle, for example to support java.util.ServiceLoader across bundles, have no specified way to do so. This specification defines a hook service that is consulted after the search order did not provide a class or resource.

listitem.para: Additive - A hook can only add classes and resources.
Wiring is authoritative - Packages a bundle imports, requires or exports are never delegated.
No Metadata - Neither the asking bundle nor the providing bundle needs to declare anything.
Extension - Hooks can be registered by framework extension bundles.
Delegation Hook - A service implementing DelegationHook.
Asking Bundle - The bundle whose class loader is asked for a class or resource.

section.title: Delegation Hook
section.para: A bundle registers a DelegationHook service. The framework calls all Delegation Hook services in service ranking order as the last step of the Overall Search Order, see .

listitem.para: findClass is called if the search order did not find the class. The first hook that returns a class wins.
findResource is called if the search order did not find the resource. The first hook that returns a URL wins.
findResources is always called. The returned URLs are appended to the resources found by the search order.

section.para: The framework must not call a hook for classes and resources in java.* packages, nor for packages that the Asking Bundle imports, requires or exports. For a resource, the package is derived from the path of the resource.

The framework must not hold any of its locks while calling a hook. It must not call a hook for the same wiring and name while that hook is running on the same thread. If a hook throws an exception, the framework must publish a Framework Event of type ERROR and continue as if the hook returned nothing.

If a class returned by a hook is defined by the class loader of another bundle, the Asking Bundle depends on that bundle for refreshing packages, in the same way as for a dynamically imported package.

Classes and resources contributed by a hook remain subject to the permissions of the bundle that provides them. A Delegation Hook may be registered by a framework extension bundle from its ExtensionBundle-Activator.

section.title: Security
section.para: Delegation Hooks are a highly privileged facility, because they can make the content of any bundle visible to any other bundle. The permission to register them should only be given to privileged bundles. The user of the hook service is the framework, so there is never a need to provide ServicePermission[..DelegationHook,GET]. Implementers must have ServicePermission[..DelegationHook,REGISTER].
